resources.string: Tarmac recognised this head unit. It reads the car’s signals from it and never sends anything to the car.
%1$s opens Tarmac when the car starts and keeps it running while the car sleeps.
To open Tarmac when the car starts, choose Tarmac as the starting app in %1$s Settings. %1$s then also keeps Tarmac running while the car sleeps.
%1$s CarPlay starts by itself and can take the iPhone before Tarmac. Turn off its automatic start in %1$s Settings.
The head unit’s Apple chip on %1$s is open to Tarmac. A change applies at the next connection. Keep %2$s CarPlay closed while Tarmac uses the chip.
The head unit’s Apple chip is on %1$s, but Android’s security policy keeps apps away from it, so Tarmac uses its own identity.
Tarmac found no %1$s, so it uses its own identity.
Tarmac could not check %1$s, so it uses its own identity.
Voice and call keys to CarPlay
While CarPlay runs, the wheel’s voice key opens Siri and its call keys answer and end CarPlay calls. Needs the Tarmac wheel keys service.
While reversing, Tarmac leaves the screen to the %1$s camera and opens CarPlay only after reverse ends.
The CAN box reports no values.
Speed %1$s km/h · Outside %2$s °C · Range %3$s km · Charge %4$s %%

Root opened the head unit’s Apple chip on %1$s. Tarmac uses it through a root helper; nothing on the system is changed. A change applies at the next connection. Keep %2$s CarPlay closed while Tarmac uses the chip.
Root could not open %1$s, so Tarmac uses its own identity.
Tarmac hands %1$s one test track (Tarmac test, CarPlay) the way %1$s’s own players do. Watch the instrument cluster or HUD. Nothing is sent until you press the button.
Some car protocols show only the active source’s track. This can switch the head unit’s audio to Tarmac.
Sent, but %1$s logged nothing about it. Try the other track record, or make Tarmac the active source.
Sends AMap’s standard guidance for about 10 seconds: turn left in 350 m onto Tarmac Street. %1$s passes it to the cluster or HUD only on CAN-box profiles that show guidance.
Sent. Watch the cluster or HUD. Without root, Tarmac cannot read %1$s’s log.
